Now Q2:

**Question:** When you save a new bookmark, what should its read state be by default?

**Why it matters:** This decides whether the unread view acts as an inbox of everything you save (so nothing is missed) or only holds items you deliberately flag. It sets the expected behavior for US5's acceptance test.

**Recommended:** Option A — a bookmarking tool's read-later queue is most useful when every newly saved item lands in "unread" automatically and you clear it as you go; this matches the workflow you described.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Every newly saved bookmark starts as **unread** (the unread view is an inbox of all new saves) |
| B | New bookmarks start as **read**; the user explicitly marks items "to read" when they want them queued |
| C | Ask/choose per save (a toggle at save time, defaulting to unread) |

You can reply with the option letter, accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
